message:
QUESTION:
Under company policy, which of the five stores should receive this year's refurbishment budget?

DATA:
Five-store retail chain, financial year 2025. A refurbishment budget is available for one store. Company policy: the budget goes to the store with the lowest annual sales per square foot of sales floor (the company's space-productivity KPI), measured on a full-year basis.

| Store | Annual sales 2025 | Sales floor area (sq ft) | Gross internal area incl. stockrooms (sq ft) |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | 10,000 |
| South | £3.6m | 15,000 | 18,000 |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | 9,000 |
| West | £2.1m | 10,000 | 12,000 |
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | 14,000 |

Annual sales 2024: North £2.3m, South £3.5m, East £1.7m, West £2.9m, Central £4.0m. Floor areas were the same in 2024.

Operations note: West was closed from January to March 2025 (3 months) for flood repairs, so its 2025 sales cover 9 trading months. All other stores traded for all 12 months in both years. The flood repairs were covered by insurance and did not change the store's layout.

KNOWN FLAWS:
F1. [method] The company KPI is sales per square foot of sales floor, not gross internal area. Using gross area changes the densities and their relative gaps. CORRECTION: Sales-floor densities (2025 as reported): North £300, South £240, East £300, West £210, Central £350.
F2. [calculation] £4.2m / 14,000 = £300, not £320 (even on the draft's gross-area basis). CORRECTION: £300 per sq ft gross (or £350 on sales floor). Central is 50%, not 'roughly 60%', above South and East on gross area.
F3. [omission] Ignores that West traded for only 9 months in 2025 (flood closure), while policy requires a full-year basis. CORRECTION: Annualised West sales = £2.1m × 12/9 = £2.8m: £280 per sq ft of sales floor. The lowest full-year density is South at £240, so South gets the budget.
F4. [misreport] In 2024 West had the second-highest density (£2.9m / 10,000 = £290 per sq ft of sales floor). South was the weakest (£3.5m / 15,000 = £233). CORRECTION: West was not weak in 2024. Its 2025 'decline' is the closure, so there is no trend case for West; South was weakest in both years.

EXTENSIONS:
- Show the decision is robust: South is lowest on sales-floor density in both 2024 (£233) and annualised 2025 (£240), while on gross area South and East tie at £200 once West is annualised (£233), which shows why the KPI's definition matters.
- Check West's post-reopening run rate (monthly sales April-December vs the same months of 2024) to confirm that annualising is fair, i.e. that West did not reopen with depressed trade.
- Consider return on refurbishment rather than lowest density alone: e.g. South's large floor (15,000 sq ft) means each £10/sq ft uplift is worth £150,000 a year, more than in any other store.

FINAL VERSION:
# Refurbishment budget: store productivity review (revised)

## Recommendation

**Under company policy, the refurbishment budget should go to South.** South has the lowest full-year sales per square foot of sales floor, at £240. The previous draft recommended West, but that result came from two errors in method, not from West's trading.

## What was wrong with the previous analysis

1. **Wrong denominator.** The policy KPI is sales per square foot of **sales floor**. The draft used gross internal area, including stockrooms. That may be a reasonable measure of property cost, but it is not the measure the policy specifies. It also changes the ranking, because the share of space given to stockrooms differs by store (from 67% sales floor at East to 86% at Central).
2. **No full-year adjustment for West.** The policy requires a full-year basis. West traded for only 9 months in 2025 because of the flood closure. Comparing its 9 months of sales with other stores' 12 months makes it look about 25% weaker than it was.
3. **The trend claims were wrong.**
   - The "fall from £2.9m to £2.1m, a drop of more than a quarter" compares 12 months of trading with 9. On an annualised basis, West's sales moved from £2.9m to about £2.8m, a decline of roughly 3%.
   - "West was also the weakest store last year" is false on either measure. In 2024 West had the **highest** sales-floor density in the chain apart from Central (£290). On gross area it was also mid-table, with East lowest.
4. **The diagnosis was wrong.** The draft treated West's 2025 figure as evidence of a local trading problem that refurbishment could fix. The shortfall is explained by a closure that insurance covered. The repairs did not change the store's layout, so they were not a refurbishment either.

## Sales density, 2025 (policy basis: sales floor area, full year)

West's sales are annualised pro rata: £2.1m × 12/9 = £2.8m.

| Store | 2025 sales (full-year basis) | Sales floor (sq ft) | Sales per sq ft | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Central | £4.2m | 12,000 | £350 | 1 |
| North | £2.4m | 8,000 | £300 | 2= |
| East | £1.8m | 6,000 | £300 | 2= |
| West | £2.8m (annualised; actual £2.1m over 9 months) | 10,000 | £280 | 4 |
| **South** | **£3.6m** | **15,000** | **£240** | **5 (lowest)** |

South is the lowest, £40 per sq ft (about 14%) below West, the next-weakest store.

## Robustness checks

- **Seasonality in the West adjustment.** Pro-rata annualising assumes January to March is an average quarter. West would only fall below South if its annualised sales were under £2.4m. That would mean January to March normally brings in less than about 12.5% of its annual sales, against 25% on a pro-rata basis. That level of seasonality is implausible for a general retailer. If monthly sales history for West is available, it should be used to confirm this, but it is very unlikely to change the answer.
- **Consistency with 2024.** On the same basis, 2024 densities were: Central £333, West £290, North £288, East £283, **South £233**. South was the lowest in 2024 as well, so the result is not a one-year effect.
- **Unadjusted figures.** If West's 9-month sales were wrongly treated as a full year, West would come out at £210 and appear lowest. That is the error the policy's "full-year basis" wording is designed to prevent.

## Other context

- On a like-for-like basis, every store except West grew in 2025: North +4%, South +3%, East +6%, Central +5%.
- Reported chain sales fell from £14.4m to £14.1m. On a full-year-equivalent basis they rose to about £14.8m (+3%). The reported decline comes entirely from West's closure.
- South is the largest store by floor area but only the second-largest by sales. This suggests space that is under-used rather than a store in decline. A refurbishment brief could therefore look at layout, how the space is allocated, and possibly re-letting or reducing the sales floor, as well as a cosmetic refresh.
- West has no space-productivity case for the budget. Its pre-closure performance was strong. Any post-reopening concerns, such as customers who may not have come back after the closure, would be a separate trading question.

## Measuring the result

Compare South's sales density in the 12 months after the works with its pre-works level (about £233 to £240 per sq ft) and with the chain's average change over the same period, so that chain-wide trends are not credited to the refurbishment. If the works change the size of the sales floor, recalculate the KPI using the new area. Schedule the works outside peak trading periods, and treat any months of partial trading the same way West's closure was treated here: annualise them, not compare them raw.
